title: Patron's Guide: Headroom Allowed for Grain Already Hauled Against an Application
content:
**Why is a credit given for grain already hauled?** The hauled-load credit allows headroom on Grain Marketing Contracts for grain the member has already hauled against the application, whose tickets stand held against the contract until it is countersigned and whose bushels come off the contract only as loads are applied to it; every load standing against the contract counts here, whatever the disposition.

**How much is the credit?**

- Where four or more loads stand against the contract and the bushels they carry reach the smallest contract the member's marketing programme will write, the credit is 250 bushels for each load standing.
- Where loads stand against the contract but that pair of conditions is not met, the credit is 100 bushels for each load standing.
- Where no load stands against the contract, no hauled-load credit is added.

**Which loads count?** Every load standing against the contract, whatever the disposition: a load the member directed to the contract at the scale and a load the member ran straight through to the buyer both count, and both count wherever the load was received.

**What is the smallest contract each programme writes?**

| Programme | Smallest contract (bushels) |
|---|---|
| Spot Cash Delivery Ticket | 1 |
| Forward Cash Sale Contract | 1000 |
| Basis Fixed Contract | 5000 |
| Hedge-to-Arrive Contract | 5000 |
| Delayed Price Agreement | 1000 |
| Minimum Price Contract | 5000 |
| Managed Accumulator Program | 10000 |

**Is the credit per load or per contract?** Per load. Five loads reaching the first band carry 1,250 bushels of credit between them; five loads that do not reach it carry 500.

**A hypothetical case.** Six loads stand against an application on a Hedge-to-Arrive Contract, carrying 7,200 net bushels between them. Four or more loads stand and the bushels they carry reach that programme's smallest contract of 5000, so the credit is 250 bushels on each of the six loads, being 1,500 bushels. Had three loads stood, carrying the same bushels, the credit would be 100 bushels on each of the three, being 300 bushels.
